baseline.note: Probed on 2026-11-04 against this exact build; the image is the artifact the context module reads.

specs.title: Element-wise INSERT target `col[i]` is rejected by the SQL grammar
specs.statement: INSERT ... (c1, arr[i], c3) VALUES (...) must be accepted by the parser and resolved as a partial write of element i of the ARRAY column arr. Today the statement fails in the grammar before name resolution runs.

evidence.observed:
ERROR 1064: ... near '[1], bar[2], bar[3], bar[4], label) VALUES (...)' at line 1
ERROR 1064: ... near '[2]) VALUES (3, 'row3', 52)' at line 1
evidence.repro:
create table w(id int not null primary key, slots array(int), bar array(int), label varchar(8));
insert into w(id, bar[1], bar[2], label) values (1, 40, 50, 'row1');

sources.note: The INSERT target list only admits plain column references; no ARRAY element form exists.
`[1]` parses as an ARRAY literal, so `bar[1]` leaves the token `[1]` before the next `,`.
Every INSERT form shares this target-list production.

specs.title: Element-wise UPDATE target `col[i]` is rejected by the SQL grammar
specs.statement: UPDATE t SET arr[i] = v must be accepted and must rewrite only element i of arr in every updated row.

evidence.observed: ERROR 1064: ... near '[3] = 7 WHERE id = 1' at line 1

sources.note: The assignment target is a bare column reference only.
List of update_asgn_factor for `UPDATE ... SET` and `INSERT ... SET`.

specs.title: Element-wise DELETE predicate `col[i] = v` is rejected by the SQL grammar
specs.statement: The predicate `arr[i] = v` must be usable wherever a boolean expression is allowed (starting with DELETE ... WHERE) and must select the rows whose element i equals v.

sources.note: `slots[3]` reaches the expression grammar as a column followed by an ARRAY literal.
DELETE reuses the normal predicate/scan path, so one expression form covers the whole family.

specs.title: Element reads `col[i]` are unsupported in expressions
specs.statement: `SELECT arr[i]` and any expression that reads one element must be supported once ARR-005 provides the node.

evidence.observed: ERROR 1064: ... near '[2] FROM dual' at line 1

sources.note: An ARRAY node can only become the N_ARRAY function; it has no 'value of my first element' meaning.

specs.title: Parser must expose an ARRAY_INDEX node for `col[i]`
specs.statement: The grammar must build an element-access node for `<column-ref> '[' expr ']'`, and that node must be distinguishable from the ARRAY literal node `'[' expr_list ']'`.

evidence.observed: No node exists: `SELECT slots[1] ...` fails in the lexer/parser, and the only node the grammar can build for brackets is T_FUN_SYS_ARRAY (1737), which is the ARRAY literal.

sources.note: The ARRAY literal node; there is no companion element-access node.
Potential anchor: element access takes a column reference as its base.
The ARRAY literal production that currently swallows `[i]` after a column.

specs.title: The element-access expression reads `col[i]` in SELECT
specs.statement: `SELECT arr[i] FROM t` must return the element at 1-based position i, and must return NULL when i is out of range or NULL.

evidence.repro: select slots[1] from t where t.slots = [1,2,3,4];

sources.note: Expression operators are registered here; a function-grade operator can live in sysfunc.
ARRAY helpers (array_first, array_map, reverse) live here and show the expected shape for array-aware evaluation.

specs.title: Writes targets resolve through the shared `insert_columns` / assignment path
specs.statement: Element targets must be accepted by the resolver entry points that already validate INSERT target columns and UPDATE assignment columns, and an out-of-range element index must raise a clear error instead of silently appending.

sources.note: The single validation gate for INSERT target lists.
INSERT resolution entry that reaches the shared validation gate.

specs.title: Existing ARRAY literal, helper and vector overload rules keep today's results
specs.statement: ARRAY literal + ARRAY literal with different cardinality keeps its current error, ARRAY +/- scalar keeps its current error, the lambda helpers must reject a scalar number input and `reverse()` must keep its scalar and array behaviour; none of these may change to support element access, and none may stop working.

evidence.observed:
array(1,2)+array(3) -> 7602 'array type mismatch found between definition and data'
array(1,2)+3 -> 5083 'Invalid data type for the operation'
array_map(x->x, 5) -> 5083 'Invalid data type for the operation'
array_first(x->x>0, 5) -> 5083 'Invalid data type for the operation'
reverse(array(1,2)) -> '[2,1]'
reverse('abc') -> 'cba'

sources.note: The shared arithmetic overload used by every array arithmetic test.
Lambda helper argument typing.
`reverse()` is the only existing function that switches behaviour on the argument being an ARRAY.

specs.title: Deprecated vector/index paths and current ARRAY DML forms must keep working
specs.statement: `analyze table`, of an ARRAY column, the array_arith_op / array_ddl suites' current statements, and the vector `l2_distance` ordering must keep their current results; adding element access must not disturb them.

evidence.observed: tests/seatbelt/array_arith_op_mysql.test + array_ddl_mysql.test pass on the baseline build
evidence.repro: run tools/deploy/mysql_test/test_suite/array from the current tree

sources.note: DDL and DML shapes that must keep working: [1,2], array(1,2), [[..]], insert into arr_t1(c2) values([57584]).
Arithmetic result and overflow error codes that must keep working.
